concept: Bucket catalog memory and closure reasons
summary: Source-anchored research for Bucket catalog memory and closure reasons. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: cacheSizeBytes in that formula is the configured WiredTiger cache size: getStorageCacheSizeBytes() multiplies getCacheSizeMB(), which returns the configured _wtConfig.cacheSizeMB. It is not live cache occupancy, eviction state or dirty ratio. 'Cache pressure' in kCachePressure and numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure therefore names a computed budget, not an observed eviction condition. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries_write_util.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/wiredtiger_kv_engine.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp

A mongod restart is a temporary workaround: it closes all buckets and resets the catalog, and one forum user reported relief for about three days after each restart (Feb 22, 2024). (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863

Restarting mongod is a mitigation, not a fix. It closes all buckets and resets the bucket catalog, but users report relief lasting about three days (forum 2024-02-22) or restarting servers daily (feedback 2024-02-22). SERVER-89233 is fixed from 8.0.5 (also 8.1.0-rc0). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md ; https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863 ; https://feedback.mongodb.com/ideas/CUSTOMER-I-7595

The bucket catalog is one mongod-wide in-memory structure (a ServiceContext decoration) split into 32 hard-coded lock stripes. It tracks open and archived buckets. mongod's tracking allocator measures its memory, and serverStatus reports that figure as bucketCatalog.memoryUsage. A mongod restart discards the catalog and closes all buckets. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/global_bucket_catalog.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_server_status.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md

When catalog memory exceeds the threshold (timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold), expireIdleBuckets works through idle buckets. It archives an idle open bucket that can still take inserts and increments numBucketsArchivedDueToMemoryThreshold. It closes an idle bucket whose state conflicts with insertions and increments numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold; cleared or frozen buckets are only removed. If memory is still high, it closes archived buckets, also counted in numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold. The work per call is capped by timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMaxCountPerAttempt (default 3), though the loop condition is numExpired <= the limit, so a call can handle one more than the parameter value. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl

determineRolloverReason checks in this order and returns the first match: time span forward, time backward, document count, size or cache pressure, schema incompatibility. Schema change therefore registers only when the earlier checks pass, and a comment in the function records an earlier bug where skipping the size check also skipped later checks and let mixed-schema data into a bucket. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp

A backward timestamp increments numBucketsArchivedDueToTimeBackward. The counter numBucketsClosedDueToTimeBackward is no longer emitted: SERVER-89158 (fixed in 8.0.0-rc7 and 8.1.0-rc0) removed it because it never rose above zero. The manual's serverStatus and collStats pages still list it. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89158 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collStats.md

Symptom: nearly one bucket per document, avgNumMeasurementsPerCommit near 1, and a very large numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure, usually days after startup. SERVER-89233 (sharded cluster, 7.0.4 and 7.0.5, created 2024-04-10) describes it. A forum poster saw bucketCount 25,000 and 17 measurements per commit when loading a collection on a fresh server, but about 420,000 buckets, 1 measurement per commit and about 415,000 cache-pressure closures when loading it after other collections (Oct 19, 2023). Replies through Mar 2025 report the same. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233 ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863

SERVER-89233 is Fixed in 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0 (resolved 2024-10-03). The ticket requested backports to 8.0 and 7.0, but it lists no 7.0.x fix version as of 2026-10-20. Commit 46e8db22 ('Track cardinality per-collection for time-series') replaced the catalog-wide uint32 counter numberOfActiveBuckets with per-collection numActiveBuckets gauges and subtracts a dropped collection's gauge from the global one. Neither the ticket nor the commit states a root cause. The reporter also hit the problem after dropping and re-inserting collections. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233 ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/commit/46e8db22.patch

Dropping a collection, moving a chunk, or an election can cause a set of buckets to be cleared, with their removal deferred; stateManagement.trackedClearOperations counts these deferred clears. A conflicting operation such as a chunk migration or an update can close a bucket. Direct writes such as updates and deletes are tracked for conflict management in stateManagement.bucketsManaged, and the writer must notify the BucketCatalog through handleDirectWrite or clear. stateManagement.currentEra starts at 0 and increments when a bucket is cleared. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md

In MongoDB's internal medium- and high-cardinality workloads, buckets close because time moves forward, so raising the count or size limits would not help them (SERVER-88644, Backlog, created 2024-03-27). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Each internal rollover reason maps to one of three actions. Count, schema change, cache pressure and size hard-close the bucket. A timestamp past the bucket's time span (time forward) soft-closes it, so it stays eligible for reopening. A timestamp earlier than the bucket's minimum time (time backward) archives it. If the bucket still holds uncommitted measurements, the server records the reason and acts when the last batch commits. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/rollover.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/rollover.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp

expireIdleBuckets works in this order, and only while catalog memory usage is above the memory usage threshold. It archives each idle open bucket that can still accept inserts and counts it in numBucketsArchivedDueToMemoryThreshold. It removes a cleared or frozen idle bucket with no counter. It closes any other idle bucket and counts it in numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold. When the idle list is empty it closes archived entries and counts each in numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold. The server runs this only when it allocates a new bucket or loads a reopened bucket into the catalog. Both loops share one counter and stop once it exceeds timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMaxCountPerAttempt (default 3). Because the test is <=, up to 4 expiries can happen per call. Code reading of the pinned source commit. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl

The cache term is the configured WiredTiger cache size (storage engine getCacheSizeMB() x 1 MiB), not live cache occupancy. The bucket term is the process-wide count of open plus archived buckets across every time series collection (serverStatus bucketCatalog.numBuckets). numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure therefore reflects a capacity ratio, not observed cache eviction, and a busy collection can shrink the cap of a quiet one. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries_write_util.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187

Since 6.1.0 (SERVER-66683) a bucket that could still accept measurements but would close because of memory pressure or out-of-order inserts is archived instead. The per-stripe archive keeps only a hash of the bucket key and the bucket _id. A memory-driven closure is not permanent: the README says an archived entry dropped for memory remains eligible for query-based reopening, which needs a {metaField: 1, timeField: 1} index (created by default for collections made on 6.3 or later). Without that index no query-based reopening happens and a new bucket opens. (high confidence) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-66683 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/README.md

serverStatus().bucketCatalog (since 5.0) is process-wide. It reports numBuckets (open plus archived), numOpenBuckets, numIdleBuckets, numArchivedBuckets (numBuckets minus numOpenBuckets, floored at 0), memoryUsage in bytes, one counter per closure or archive reason, and a stateManagement block. Per-collection counters appear in $collStats storageStats output for time series collections. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_server_status.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md

Inference, not stated by MongoDB: the divisor counts active buckets process-wide (globalExecutionStats.numActiveBuckets), so counts that were not released when a collection was dropped would inflate it and shrink every collection's cap. Consistent evidence: SERVER-89233 reports the symptom after deleting and re-inserting time series collections; the fix commit is titled 'Track cardinality per-collection for time-series' and adds removeCollectionExecutionGauges, which subtracts a dropped collection's active-bucket count from the global gauge; a community user reports that restarting resolves the issue for about 3 days. The ticket page states no root cause. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/commit/46e8db22d75751f6469d95f87a5ad700f51264d6.patch ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863

Workaround for a collapsing cap: raise timeseriesBucketMinSize toward timeseriesBucketMaxSize (SERVER-105187, an unresolved Backlog ticket last updated 2025-07-14 that asks for a configurable constant in the dynamic bucketing calculation). The parameter is startup-only in 7.0.0 and startup-or-runtime in 7.3.0 and 8.0.0 (the 8.0.x scope beyond 8.0.0 was not pinned). Cost: SERVER-69899 introduced dynamic bucket sizing in 6.2 because, with many active buckets at the full default size, the WT cache could be exceeded and each document write would trigger a write to disk. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r7.0.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r7.3.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899

Before SERVER-95511, timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold defaulted to 0, which meant 2.5% of system memory, and positive values were bytes (7.0 branch). SERVER-95511 (fixed in 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0) changed the default to 5. Values 1 to 100 now mean a percentage of system memory, values above 100 mean bytes, and zero or negative values fall back to 5%. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v7.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95511

timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold and timeseriesSideBucketCatalogMemoryUsageThreshold can be set at startup or at runtime; timeseriesBucketMaxCount is startup-only. Alibaba Cloud's MongoDB 8.0 parameter list agrees: no restart for the two thresholds, restart required for timeseriesBucketMaxCount (range 1 to 10000). The side catalog threshold takes bytes only (default 100 MB); Alibaba limits it to 52428800 through 209715200. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/parameters-available-in-mongodb-8-0

Work out the expiry threshold as a percentage of total system RAM: 5% from 8.0.5, 2.5% before. Compare it with serverStatus().bucketCatalog.memoryUsage. Expiry runs only on bucket allocation or reopen, so a quiet node can keep memoryUsage above the threshold. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.5/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.4/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp

In a 7.0.2 replica set (Feb 2024), about 120.4 million documents produced 12,151,933 buckets (about 9.9 documents per bucket, avgBucketSize 4849) on a 128 GB host and 1,508,453 buckets (about 79.9 per bucket, avgBucketSize 13428) on a 16 GB host. The 16 GB host reported numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure 1,050,343; the 128 GB host's closure counters were all zero. The larger host got the smaller buckets, so cache size alone does not predict bucket density. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold sets the catalog's memory budget and can be changed at startup or at runtime. From 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0 (SERVER-95511) it defaults to 5. A value from 1 to 100 means a percentage of system memory. A value above 100 means bytes. Zero or a negative value resets to the 5% default. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95511

The manual's bucketing page says the bucket catalog's default total memory allocation is 2.5% of available system memory. That matches the source in 8.0.4 (the idle-bucket expiry threshold defaults to 2.5% of system memory). In 8.0.5 the source default changed to 5% (SERVER-95511, fixed in 8.1.0-rc0 and 8.0.5), and Alibaba Cloud's MongoDB 8.0 parameter table also lists 5%. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.4/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.5/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/user-guide/parameters-available-in-mongodb-8-0

Suggested diagnostic order for too many small buckets (synthesis of the sources): (1) per collection, compare timeseries.bucketCount with documents inserted and read avgNumMeasurementsPerCommit; (2) see which numBucketsClosedDueTo* counter dominates; (3) if CachePressure, compare the node-wide numActiveBuckets x 2 x 128,000 (the default timeseriesBucketMaxSize) with the WiredTiger cache size, because the cache-derived bucket size limit is cache size / (2 x active buckets); the SERVER-89233 report (affects 7.0.4 and 7.0.5, fixed in 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0) describes counts staying high after a time series collection was dropped; (4) if MemoryThreshold counters rise, compare memoryUsage with the timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold (5% of system memory by default from 8.0.5, 2.5% in 8.0.4 and 7.0) and raise it; (5) reduce metaField cardinality. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.4/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.5/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233 ; https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863

The manual lists six circumstances that close a bucket: time moving past the bucket span (forward or backward), the document limit (default 1000), the storage size limit (default 125 KiB, with a 12 MiB allowance for buckets under 10 documents, and the active bucket set not fitting the allowed storage engine cache size), the catalog exceeding its total memory allocation, a conflicting operation such as a chunk migration or update, and a mongod restart. (high confidence)

The cache-derived bucket size limit is storageCacheSizeBytes / (2 * activeBuckets), raised to at least timeseriesBucketMinSize (default 5120 bytes) and capped at timeseriesBucketMaxSize (default 128000 bytes, about 125 KB). An active bucket is one that is either archived or open. If a measurement would push a bucket past the limit, rollover is kSize when the effective limit equals timeseriesBucketMaxSize and kCachePressure otherwise. Exception: a bucket with fewer than timeseriesBucketMinCount (default 10) measurements is kept open for large measurements until it passes a higher absolute ceiling. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/README.md

Default limits on master: timeseriesBucketMaxCount 1000 measurements, timeseriesBucketMaxSize 128000 bytes, timeseriesBucketMinCount 10, timeseriesBucketMinSize 5120 bytes, timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMaxCountPerAttempt 3, timeseriesSideBucketCatalogMemoryUsageThreshold 104857600 bytes. A bucket with fewer than 10 measurements may grow past the size limit, up to 12 MiB. numBucketsKeptOpenDueToLargeMeasurements counts those buckets. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket.h ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md

serverStatus().bucketCatalog.numBuckets is the node-wide gauge of active buckets (open plus archived). The dynamic size limit uses the same gauge. numArchivedBuckets is numBuckets minus numOpenBuckets, clamped at zero. The bucketCatalog section returns an empty document while the catalog has no per-collection stats entries, that is, before any time series collection is used after startup. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_server_status.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md

timeseriesBucketMinSize (default 5120 bytes, settable at startup and at runtime) is the floor of the cache-derived limit. SERVER-82798 (fixed in 7.0.4 and 7.2.0-rc0) made the dynamic calculation respect it. SERVER-105187 (Backlog, created 2025-05-17) says that raising it up to timeseriesBucketMaxSize effectively turns dynamic bucketing off, and proposes making the factor of 2 configurable. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-82798 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187

With default limits, the dynamic limit starts to shrink buckets once active buckets exceed cacheSizeBytes / 256000, and it reaches the 5120-byte floor above cacheSizeBytes / 10240. For an 8 GiB WiredTiger cache those points are about 33,500 and about 839,000 active buckets. Compare serverStatus().bucketCatalog.numBuckets with these values. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_server_status.cpp

numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure counts buckets closed because their size exceeds the bucket catalog's dynamic bucket size limit, derived from available storage engine cache size and numBuckets. numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold and numBucketsArchivedDueToMemoryThreshold count buckets closed or archived because the set of active buckets didn't fit within the allowed bucket catalog cache size. numBucketsClosedDueToTimeForward counts buckets closed because a document's timeField was after the maximum time of the open buckets, with bucket bounds determined by granularity. numBucketsClosedDueToSchemaChange counts buckets closed because an incoming document's schema was incompatible with the open bucket. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md

Active-bucket cardinality is node-wide. SERVER-105187 says the dynamic calculation 'combines the global cardinality of buckets across all collections', and current master code passes catalog.globalExecutionStats.numActiveBuckets to the cache-derived bucket max size calculation. Many collections can therefore shrink the size limit for new buckets in all of them. A forum poster (March 3, 2025) noted that timeseries data is in some cases used as collection iterations rather than a single collection, in a thread reporting small buckets and cache pressure. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863

Raising timeseriesBucketMinSize to timeseriesBucketMaxSize switches off dynamic sizing but trades smaller buckets for WiredTiger cache risk. SERVER-69899 (fixed in 6.2.0-rc0) added the limit because many active buckets at the full 125 KiB could exceed the cache and make each document write trigger a disk write. Compare active buckets times bucket size with the cache before disabling it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899

MongoDB engineers call the old 2.5% catalog memory default conservative and note that users often need to change the memory parameters. SERVER-95510 (created 2024-10-03, closed as a duplicate of SERVER-95511) says that raising the limit in many user deployments since 5.0 improved performance. MongoDB's docs list exceeding the bucket catalog's allowed total memory allocation as a reason buckets are closed. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95510 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md

The manual lists six top-level closure circumstances: time moving forward or backward past the covered span; the document limit (default 1000); the storage size limit (default 125KiB, or with fewer than 10 documents the bucket may stay open until 12MiB, and also when the set of active buckets doesn't fit the storage engine cache); the bucket catalog exceeding its total memory allocation; a conflicting operation such as a chunk migration or update; and a mongod restart. The defaults match timeseriesBucketMaxCount 1000, timeseriesBucketMaxSize 128000 bytes (125KB) and timeseriesBucketMinCount 10 in the server source. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl

Catalog-memory expiry and cache-derived size rollover are distinct paths. When catalog memory exceeds timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold, eligible idle open buckets are archived and numBucketsArchivedDueToMemoryThreshold increases. If pressure remains, archived entries can be removed and numBucketsClosedDueToMemoryThreshold increases. A separate size limit derived from storage cache bytes and active-bucket count can trigger numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure when a measurement would exceed the effective cap, subject to large-measurement and minimum-count exceptions. These counters describe different mechanisms. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md

Through 8.0.4 the same parameter took bytes only, and its default of 0 resolved to about 2.5% of system memory (the code multiplies system MB by 25 x 1024, which is 2.44%). SERVER-61195 (fixed 5.0.6 and 5.2.0) replaced an earlier fixed 100 MB limit with one that scales with RAM. SERVER-95510 recorded the default as 'a conservative 2.5%' in October 2024 and proposed 5%. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.4/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries_global_options.cpp ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95511 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-61195 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95510

Since 6.2.0 (SERVER-69899) the server lowers the maximum bucket size dynamically so that all active buckets together use no more than half the WiredTiger cache. In current server source the limit is cacheBytes / (2 x activeBuckets), raised to at least timeseriesBucketMinSize (default 5120 bytes) and capped at timeseriesBucketMaxSize (default 128000 bytes). With no active buckets the static maximum applies. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl

When a measurement would push a bucket past its effective size limit, the server reports kSize if the effective limit equals timeseriesBucketMaxSize and kCachePressure if the cache-derived limit is lower. A bucket with fewer than timeseriesBucketMinCount (default 10) measurements may grow past that limit, up to the smaller of 12 MiB and the cache-derived limit, and is counted once in numBucketsKeptOpenDueToLargeMeasurements. Beyond that ceiling it closes as kSize or kCachePressure by the same rule. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl

determineRolloverReason checks in this order: time forward, time backward, document count, size or cache pressure, then schema change. Each check returns only when it finds a rollover is needed, so the first match wins. A measurement that exceeds the size limit and is also schema-incompatible is reported as size or cache pressure. Exception: a bucket with fewer than timeseriesBucketMinCount measurements is kept open for large measurements, and then falls through to the schema check. (Master branch code reading.) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp

Reported failure mode: buckets shrink to about one measurement each. A 128 GB host with 50 time series collections showed bucketCount near 420,000, avgNumMeasurementsPerCommit 1 and about 415,000 numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure for one collection (forum, 2023-10-19, version not stated). A 7.0.2 replica set with 128 GB nodes saw cache-pressure closures grow until restart (forum, 2024-02-19). SERVER-89233 reproduced 'bucket count equals document count' on a 7.0.4 sharded cluster several days after startup, and again after dropping and recreating collections. (high confidence) Sources: https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863 ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/bsonobjtoolarge-error-after-restarting-mongod-instance-for-timeseries-data/267023 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233

Before the SERVER-82798 fix (fixed in 7.0.4 and 7.2.0-rc0, resolved 2023-11-07), the dynamic bucket max size calculation did not respect the time-series bucket minimum size and could produce a small maximum size, leaving buckets with few measurements. Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-82798

To raise catalog memory, set timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold at runtime. From 8.0.5 the value can be a percentage of system memory (1-100) rather than bytes, so the budget scales with the cluster, for example under autoscaling. SERVER-95510 says MongoDB has raised these limits in many user deployments since 5.0. SERVER-95511 warns that if a user scales down without adjusting fixed byte parameters, they risk OOM errors. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r8.0.5/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95511 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95510

timeseriesSideBucketCatalogMemoryUsageThreshold is a byte budget (default 104,857,600, startup or runtime) for a separate side bucket catalog. The IDL and Alibaba Cloud describe it as the level above which idle buckets in that catalog expire. SERVER-75176 (7.2.0-rc0) added a memory limit on the side catalog used by each time series update command and says an update over the limit should return an error; the ticket does not name the parameter. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/parameters-available-in-mongodb-8-0 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-75176

Which closure reason dominates depends on write rate and span. In MongoDB's blog tests (M30, 10 devices) fast writers closed buckets on size or count, and slow writers closed them on time span. Per the serverStatus docs: Size and Count are expected at high rates; TimeForward counts buckets closed because a document arrived with a timeField value after the maximum time of all open buckets for that metaField value; SchemaChange means an incoming document's schema was incompatible with the open bucket; CachePressure means a bucket exceeded the dynamic cache-derived size limit; MemoryThreshold means active buckets didn't fit within the allowed bucket catalog cache size. Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/a-practical-study-of-mongodb-time-series-bucket-behavior ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md

The starting timestamp of a new bucket is rounded down based on the collection's granularity, or by bucketRoundingSeconds when custom bucketing is used (6.3+). This handles cases where documents with out-of-order timestamps arrive in close succession. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-granularity.md

bucketCatalog.stateManagement.currentEra starts at 0 and increments when a bucket is cleared. trackedClearOperations counts clear operations whose bucket removal was deferred, for example after a collection drop, a chunk migration or an election. Conflicting operations that change on-disk bucket state, such as chunk migrations or updates, may close affected buckets to prevent inconsistencies. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md

mongod keeps one in-memory bucket catalog for all time series collections on the node. It holds the open buckets and a small record for each archived bucket, split across 32 hash stripes; a given metaField value always maps to the same stripe. Restarting mongod closes all buckets and resets the catalog. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/ ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187

expireIdleBuckets is called in two places in bucket_catalog_internal.cpp on master: loadBucketIntoCatalog (loading a reopened bucket) and allocateBucket (allocating a new bucket). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp

Each rollover reason maps to one action. kTimeForward soft-closes the bucket, which stays eligible for reopening. kTimeBackward archives the bucket and keeps a small in-memory record. kCount, kSchemaChange, kCachePressure and kSize hard-close the bucket permanently. Archiving increments numBucketsArchivedDueToTimeBackward; each other reason increments its own numBucketsClosedDueTo counter. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/rollover.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/rollover.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md

Catalog memory is measured with mongod's tracking allocator and reported in bytes as serverStatus().bucketCatalog.memoryUsage. timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold, if set to a number between 1 and 100, is a percentage of system memory (default 5), not of the WiredTiger cache; a value above 100 is interpreted as a number of bytes. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl

Closure counters appear node-wide in serverStatus().bucketCatalog and per collection under timeseries in collStats (db.collection.stats()). Both come from appendExecutionStatsToBuilder, which emits numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure and numBucketsClosedDueToSchemaChange. The collStats command reference's timeseries example lists neither counter, although the $collStats page example does. The SERVER-89233 reporter read numBucketsClosedDueToCachePressure from stats(). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/execution_stats.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_server_status.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collStats.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233

Bucket count follows distinct metaField values. Fine-grained or changing metaField values create many sparsely packed, short-lived buckets, which raises catalog cardinality. Choose a stable, coarse metaField and a granularity (or bucketMaxSpanSeconds) that matches the measurement interval. The manual warns that granularity 'seconds' on data arriving every 5 minutes gives multiple buckets per polling interval, many holding a single document. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-best-practices.md

Insert with insertMany, group measurements with the same metaField in the same batch, and set ordered to false (manual). The server design notes say insertMany batches are organized by meta value and sorted ascending by time; earlier versions targeted buckets per measurement in the order the client gave, which produced very sub-optimal bucketing for time-descending batches. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-best-practices/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/README.md

Archiving keeps a small in-memory record, so a later measurement that fits can reopen the on-disk bucket cheaply. If no record exists, the server queries the bucket collection for a reopening candidate. numBucketsReopened, numBucketsFetched, numBucketQueriesFailed and numBucketReopeningsFailed show how well reopening works. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md

Query-based reopening needs the {metaField: 1, timeField: 1} index, which the server creates by default for time series collections created in 6.3 and later. Without that index the server does not use query-based reopening. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Inserting a measurement whose data is of a different type than the open bucket's data makes the bucket schema-incompatible; the bucket catalog rolls the bucket over to avoid mixed-schema buckets and increments numBucketsClosedDueToSchemaChange. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md

Forum users could not find a server parameter for bucket catalog memory (Mar 3, 2025). The parameter is timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold. SERVER-95510 calls it undocumented (2024-10-03), and the current manual's bucketing page does not name it. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95510 ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md

Derived from the formula and defaults (arithmetic, not stated by MongoDB): the cap drops below the 128,000-byte static maximum once active buckets exceed cacheBytes / 256,000, and reaches the 5,120-byte floor at cacheBytes / 10,240 active buckets. Setting timeseriesBucketMinSize at or above timeseriesBucketMaxSize keeps the cap at the static maximum; SERVER-105187 calls this effectively disabling dynamic bucketing. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/35647d07bc4bc11966c90fe7100eb1db0b0ac1d9/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog_internal.cpp ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/timeseries.idl ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-105187

The manual's bucketCatalog table lists numBucketsClosedDueToTimeBackward, but current server code does not emit it: a backward timestamp archives the bucket and increments numBucketsArchivedDueToTimeBackward. The 7.0.0 source still had the Closed counter. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/r7.0.0/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/execution_stats.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/execution_stats.cpp

SERVER-89233 is fixed in 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0 and was resolved on 2024-10-03. The fix is the commit 'Track cardinality per-collection for time-series'. A backport to 8.0 and 7.0 was requested, but the ticket lists no 7.0.x fix version (last updated 2025-04-25). Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89233 ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/commit/46e8db22

The inspected manual server-parameter reference omits the time-series bucket parameters. A March 3, 2025 forum reply reported finding no catalog-memory parameter, and a February 22, 2024 feedback idea requested a bucket-memory limit. MongoDB source nevertheless documents timeseriesIdleBucketExpiryMemoryUsageThreshold. Alibaba Cloud lists that parameter in its MongoDB 8.0 table. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md ; https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/suboptimal-bucket-creation-in-timeseries-collection-due-to-cache-pressure/249863 ; https://feedback.mongodb.com/ideas/CUSTOMER-I-7595 ; https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/user-guide/parameters-available-in-mongodb-8-0

A high-cardinality metaField creates one bucket per distinct value per time window, so it produces many sparse short-lived buckets. Each one adds to the active-bucket count that divides the WiredTiger cache in the dynamic size cap and to catalog memory. SERVER-69899 was written for exactly this high-cardinality case. Keep metaField values few and stable. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-69899

A closed bucket is treated like regular persisted data. MongoDB's 2026-02-23 blog says the bucket is not pinned in memory and becomes eligible for eviction under normal WiredTiger cache behavior. Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/technical/a-practical-study-of-mongodb-time-series-bucket-behavior

SERVER-94770 (fixed 8.0.5 and 8.1.0-rc0) reduced the memory footprint of archived buckets in the BucketCatalog. The ticket has no description, so the saving is unquantified. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
